'''''Scilla hyacinthoides''''' is a [[geophyte]], native to Southern Europe to Northern Iraq. Like all [[Scilla]] it is a bulbous plant.

==Habitat==
''Scilla hyacinthoides'' is native to France including Corsica, Italy (Sardegna, Sicilia), Greece including East Aegean Islands, Yugoslavia, and the [[Middle East]] with [[Turkey]], Lebanon-Syria, Iraq and the [[Palestine (region)|Palestine region]]. It was introduced to Portugal, Spain, and Algeria, and in the US to Texas and Louisiana, as well as to South Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kew Science |title=Scilla hyacinthoides L. |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:540833-1 |access-date=2023-04-23 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

==Description==
It flowers in March to April with bluish-purple flowers on {{cvt|1–1.5|m|ft}} high flowering stalks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scilla hyacinthoides L. |url=https://flora.org.il:443/en/plants/SCIHYA/ |access-date=2023-04-23 |website=Flora of Israel and adjacent areas |language=en-US}}</ref>
